title: Cinnamon-Almond Rice Horchata with Lime Zest
summary: Toasted almonds and cinnamon soak overnight with rice and lime zest, are blended and strained, then sweetened and finished with cold milk and vanilla.
equipment: large bowl or jug (at least 2 litres)
nut-milk bag or sieve lined with a double layer of muslin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast the almonds and cinnamon in the dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring, for 5-7 minutes until fragrant and just turning golden. Toasting gives a rounder, nuttier flavour.

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Tip them into the bowl with the rice, 1 litre water and the lime zest. Cover and leave for at least 8 hours at cool room temperature or in the fridge, so the rice softens enough to blend smooth.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend everything, in 2 batches if needed, for 2-3 minutes until the rice and nuts are very finely ground.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the nut-milk bag or lined sieve into the pitcher, then squeeze firmly to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the solids.

steps.title: Sweeten and chill
steps.text: Stir in the sugar, vanilla and salt until dissolved, then the cold milk. Chill until cold.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stir well, as horchata settles, then pour over ice and dust with ground cinnamon.

tips: A nut-milk bag gives the smoothest result; muslin works but squeeze it well.
Ceylon cinnamon is softer and sweeter than cassia and crumbles more easily.
Taste before adding all the sugar if you prefer it less sweet.
For a dairy-free version, replace the milk with more water or an oat drink.
storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; stir before pouring. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
